note: Round 1 cold spec-judge BUILDER FAIL: the owner-ratified 'claim is UNCONDITIONAL on seating' decision was bound by no scenario. The Given on 'seating claims the bunker desk' read 'the standing owner exists AND no presence is bound to it' — over-specific on exactly the axis the decision rules on, so a config that runs `unit claim operator --show` first and defers to an incumbent passed the whole suite while reproducing the original incident (the desk stays bound to a dead occupant and the doorbell keeps ringing the stale pane). Rule: a Given must not gate on the axis the ratified decision rules on. Swept the other 9 new scenarios for the same shape — one instance only. Fixed by trimming the absence clause and adding the companion 'seating takes the desk even when another session already holds it'. Also split the conjoined register+claim Then into separate scenarios so a subject cannot do half the sequence and pass.

Round 1 cold spec-judge ARCHITECT FAIL: the new README prose restated contracts that already have specifying homes with their own frozen suites — kind:standing semantics, last-claim-wins, presence-resolves-live-only, the multiplexer gate and never-auto-mint (packages/cyberlegion/.agents/spec/unit/registry/), and durable-delivery-vs-best-effort-ring (packages/cyberlegion/.agents/spec/mail/doorbell/). Verified both homes carry the claims verbatim. It also contradicted this node's own Non-goals, which already places the unit/mail mechanics out of scope. Rule: a node references a contract that has a specifying home, never restates it. Swept the CR's README additions — two instances (the seat bullet and the routing-bullet extension), both fixed by replacing mechanism prose with a reference while keeping the decisions and the one load-bearing why (pane-keyed identity inherits whatever last died in that pane), which is the rationale a link cannot carry. The init-cyberlegion reference was judged a pointer, not duplication, and was kept.

Round 2 cold spec-judge BUILDER FAIL: round 1's defect MIGRATED from the Given into the When. 'seating registers this session in the hub' read `When it establishes this session's identity` — which names the act under test and hands over the verdict, when the edge is SEATING. The `--show`-then-defer config that beat round 1 passes it, since it registers happily once asked to. Consequence: claim was bound to seating but register was not. The register/claim split (itself a round-1 remediation) also opened an ORDERING hole the conjoined Then had implied — claimPresence throws 'no identity in this session' (identity.ts:254-257), so a seat-claim-register config satisfied both scenarios and breaks at runtime. Fixed with one edit closing both: When -> `Operator is seated`, Then extended with `before it claims the desk`. Lesson recorded: splitting a conjoined Then can drop an ordering constraint the conjunction was silently carrying.

Impl-gate cold judge, cross-file sweep: the CR-introduced line in plugins/cyberfleet/skills/operator/README.md collapsed the two seating guards into one fail-soft clause — 'No multiplexer, OR no standing operator in the hub: say so and dispatch anyway — routing the Council to init-cyberlegion' — merging a fail-soft branch with a fail-loud one and attaching the init-cyberlegion routing to the no-multiplexer branch, where it is meaningless. SKILL.md (the loaded subject) keeps them apart, so no frozen scenario failed; the defect was the two implementation files disagreeing about the missing-owner guard's severity. Same defect class the judge was briefed to watch for in SKILL.md, landed in the sibling file instead. Split back into two sentences with their distinct severities. SKILL.md untouched, so no scenario verdict is affected by this fix.
